summary: East India Company corporate slavery across Indian Ocean, land rent collection rights under Mughal Bengal. Distinguish orders from voyages arrived, contract consideration from revenue, and local zamindari from sovereign territory.

cases.number_is: number expressly ordered for transfer from St Helena, not independently verified transport or survival count
cases.actor: English East India Company Court of Directors
cases.evidence: peer-reviewed 2024 scholarship quotes 1687 Court of Directors letter, citing original India Office Records in footnote 37
cases.gis_note: Map point at Bencoolen denotes intended destination only; do not draw sea route or assume arrival.

cases.number_is: no verified embarked or arrived quantity
cases.evidence: peer-reviewed scholarship explicitly dates 1689 expedition organized from Madras; ship, exact departures and arrivals not extracted
cases.gis_note: Madras marker denotes organization, not actual sailing track or Madagascar landing point.

cases.amount_semantics: stated consideration in reproduced Bengali land-rent collection rights deed; NOT 1698 annual company revenue, trade profits, full value of Bengal, cost of construction, or British property purchase of all land in modern Kolkata
cases.preexisting_rights_holders: local zamindar families of Sabarna group
cases.source_cautions: Reproduced English translation of 1698 deed as printed in later reference book, not inspection of original British Museum Add.MS 24039/39. Contemporary negotiations and associated political gifts are separate transactions. Local land-revenue rights under Mughal sovereignty; exact historic boundaries NOT measured.
cases.date_conflict: Later reproductions/readings of Hijri date vary November 8, 9 or 10, 1698; use just year in map, note Cambridge 2020 narrates Mughal nishan in spring
cases.geography: three named villages on Hooghly's east side; admin modern Kolkata reference, not measured survey polygon

cases.limit: Do not repeat 'zamindari rights obtained in 1699'; they were obtained 1698. Fort construction chronology differs in published secondary accounts, use coarse year and separate from verified wall outline or full 1712 completion. No new polygon.

methods: 1687 10 enslaved people is an order, not 10 proven survivors, purchases, captured, or arrivals.
1689 Madagascar is an expedition to acquire enslaved persons with total blank and no ship GPS.
Modern Indian Ocean coerced labor included local pepper growers and Company-owned enslaved persons, but do not sum overlapping categories.
1698 Rs1300 is consideration to local rights holders in deed translation, not amount of tax extracted; 1698 nishan and Mughal sovereignty separate. No conversion to modern money.
Cited scholarship refers to original files in BL India Office Records but those manuscripts were not personally accessed.
The later 1719 Bencoolen uprising and 1704 labor demand are NOT 1600-1699 events; keep as future chapter continuation.
